data: A square plaque of marble, intact on all sides other than minor damage to the upper right corner. The edges are cut back towards the rear, and the rear is polished smooth, with an incised line marking a framing border around the rear face.
The text fills the space, with word breaks not observing line end, and the text not filling the final line.
Found by Paolo Orsi, walled into a loculus in prop. M. Sangiorgi, via A. di San Giuliano (formerly via Lincoln), Catania
Photo J. Prag, 2016-05-12, courtesy Museo di Archeologia dell'Universita di Catania
Museo di Archeologia dell'Universita di Catania

This museum is principally formed around the personal collection of Libertini, augmented by donations from Paolo Orsi and other individuals. The majority of the material seems to derive from Catania and Centuripe, but there are also finds from Megara Hyblaia and many have no clear provenance (Libertini frequently purchased on the antiquities market, as well as collecting from his own excavations). The ceramics range from prehistoric to medieval, supplemented by inscriptions, antefixes, terracotta altars, strigils, figurines, pinakes and a number of fakes. A great teaching collection

Facsimile Images

Apparatus criticus

  • Text from autopsy;
  • line.1: ΕΙΡΗΝΕΣ lapis; Εἰρην(ο)ς IGCVO 855
  • lines.4-5: μηὲν β|λάψας Manganaro, CIJud 1(2).650c, JIWE 148, Biondi-Buscemi Felici (ΜΗΛΕΝ lapis); Μηλένβι λάψας Orsi; Ferrua

English translation

Marta Fogagnolo

Eirenaios the Elder bought the place, violating the commandment in no way.

commentary

The funerary inscription presents the standard purchase formula for the tomb (ll. 2-4), with the verb ἀγοράζω in the aorist, characteristic of many inscriptions from Catania (IG XIV 538, 555, 566, IGCVO 866, IMusCatania 176, 194, 200; on the use of this verb in epitaphs with tomb-purchase formulas, see Grossi Gondi 1920, 246). Lines 4-6 have been variously interpreted: Orsi (1897, 240) read Μηλένβ|ι λάψας τὴν ἐν|τολήν in the sense of facultatem sumere, with the genitive Μηλένβι referring to the previous owner of the tomb. Manganaro (1959, 347; 1959-1960, 201-202), on the other hand, corrected this to μηὲν β|λάψας τὴν ἐν|τολήν, identifying the typically Jewish formula concerning the non-violation of the commandment (for another attestation at Catania, see IMusCatania 229 ll. 2-4 μηδὲν ζημι|ώσας τὴν ἐντολήν), and thus attributing this inscription to a Jewish milieu (cf. also BE 1960.459, 1961.882). Noy (1993, 196) identified in this ‘commandment’ aspects, not further specified, of Jewish burial law: on the connection between ἐντολή and the Jewish world, see also the epithet φιλέντολος in JIWE II 240, 281, 576. The deceased is called Εἰρῆνες, another variant of Εἰρηναῖος (Noy 1993, 195 records other possible variants, rejecting the correction found in Wessel 1989), and his name is accompanied by the title characteristic of the Christian and Jewish ecclesiastical hierarchy, presbyteros.
